Cosmology and analysis¶

Distances and power spectra, full-resolution cube statistics, HI products and skeletons.

Cosmology¶

POST /v1/cosmology/distance¶

Single redshift.

{ "redshift": 0.5, "model": "Planck18" }

POST /v1/cosmology/distance/batch¶

{ "redshifts": [0.1, 0.5, 1.0], "model": "Planck15" }

Returns distances_Mpc[] in the same order. Supported models: Planck18, Planck15, Planck13, WMAP9. Up to 100 000 redshifts; a negative or non-finite entry comes back as null at its position rather than as 0 Mpc, which would be indistinguishable from a genuine z = 0.

GET /v1/cosmology/distances¶

The same quantities for one redshift plus lookback time and the age of the universe, for an arbitrary flat-or-open LambdaCDM (H0, Om0, Ode0 as query parameters; omitted ones default to Planck18). No client binding yet — the desktop only offers the four named models above.

POST /v1/cosmology/angular_power/{dataset_id} · GET /v1/cosmology/powerspectrum/{dataset_id}¶

Azimuthally averaged 2-D power spectrum of an image plane (the GET is the spec-conformant alias of the POST; same worker).

It is a relative texture spectrum, not a calibrated Cℓ: a Hann-windowed |FFT|² with the window’s power loss corrected, no mask or beam deconvolution. calibrated is false in every response for that reason.

Returns k_bins (pixel⁻¹), ell, cl / power, cl_err, n_modes, mode_coupling, plus:

field

meaning

ell_is_angular

whether ell is an angular multipole at all. false when the header carries no celestial WCS — or when its celestial axes are not the plane that was sliced out — and ell then repeats k_bins.

pixel_scale_arcsec

the scale the conversion used, null when there was none.

The distinction matters: spatial_pixel_scale_arcsec() answers 3600″ for a header with no WCS (astropy’s one-degree-per-pixel default), so asking it unconditionally produced a multipole axis computed from a pixel size nobody had stated. cl_err is the uncertainty of THIS estimator and is null for a bin with fewer than 3 modes; judge a bin by its EFFECTIVE mode count, n_modes / mode_coupling².

Analysis¶

Implemented in backend/app/routers/analysis.py. Errors are HTTP: 422 for an unusable input, 503 for a missing optional package, 500 for an unexpected failure.

GET /v1/analysis/cube-stats/{dataset_id}¶

Whole-dataset pixel statistics on the full-resolution data (the client’s own statistics are computed on the decimated preview). Streamed out-of-core in z-slabs, so it is safe on cubes larger than memory, and cached per file (path, size, modification time; up to 64 files).

Response: valid, error, cached, total_count, valid_count, blanked_count, min, max, mean, median, std, rms, mad_sigma (1.4826 × MAD), sum, bunit, median_exact (false when the median was estimated from a strided sample).

POST /v1/analysis/hi-products/{dataset_id}¶

Optically thin HI column density and integrated HI mass from the moment-0 map.

{ "channel_start": 0, "channel_end": 0, "distance_mpc": 12.3,
  "mask_enabled": true, "threshold_value": 0.0, "threshold_auto": true,
  "rest_freq_hz": null }

The cube must be in a per-beam unit with a known beam (BMAJ/BMIN), with a velocity spectral axis or, for a frequency axis, a rest_freq_hz; otherwise 422. A non-cube dataset is 422. Masking works as for /v1/products/moment. Without a mask the integral covers every finite pixel of the channel range (noise and other sources included), and the response carries a warning saying so.

Response: valid, error, channel_start, channel_end (the clamped range used), n_channels_in_cube, beam_arcsec, beam_area_pix, mask_enabled, threshold_auto, threshold_used, n_pixels_summed, warnings, nhi_unit (cm^-2), nhi_min, nhi_max, nhi_median, integrated_flux_jy_kms, distance_mpc, hi_mass_msun, hi_mass_log10_msun (null without a distance), optically_thin (true).

POST /v1/analysis/skeleton/{dataset_id} · POST /v1/analysis/skeleton/{dataset_id}/binary · POST /v1/cosmology/skeleton/{dataset_id}¶

Morphological skeleton (filaments) or void mask of one plane. The three routes run the same computation; /v1/cosmology/skeleton is an alias kept for the cosmology grouping. Requires scikit-image (503 without it).

{ "channel": 0, "threshold": null, "mode": "skeleton",
  "smooth_sigma_pix": 0.0, "persistence_threshold": null }

Field

Meaning

channel

Plane of a cube to use

threshold

Binarisation threshold; null = mean of the finite pixels

mode

skeleton (medial-axis thinning of the bright regions) or void (skeleton of the regions below the threshold)

smooth_sigma_pix

Gaussian pre-smoothing σ in pixels; 0 disables it

persistence_threshold

Drops skeleton pixels whose intensity is below it; null disables it

JSON response: valid, error, channel, width, height, threshold (the value used), mode, smooth_sigma_pix, n_skeleton_pixels, range_min, range_max, data_base64 (float32 mask, 0 or 255) and endpoints ([row, col] pairs). /binary returns the mask as one Visivo binary frame (application/octet-stream: a 12-byte big-endian header of rows, columns and flags, then little-endian float32).
